title: Retention: effective-policy computation + evaluation library (golden tests)
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Implements the v1 retention policy effective-policy computation and evaluation library used by the control plane and enforcement workers. This PR focuses on: (1) deterministic resolution of the effective retention policy given a set of org/tenant/env/region scoped policy documents, (2) a small evaluation API to answer “what is the retention for dataset X in scope Y?” and “why?” (explain output), and (3) golden tests to lock precedence and edge-case behavior.

Context
- ENG-2911 added schema + persistence + API surfaces behind FF; this PR adds the core computation/eval layer that downstream services will call.
- The output of computeEffectivePolicy() is intended to be used by: audit log retention worker, telemetry TTL configuration, Console “effective policy” view, and compliance evidence generation.

What’s in
- Precedence rules (implemented + tested):
  - Base defaults (service-provided) < org policy < tenant policy < env overrides < region overrides
  - Within a scope: more specific selector wins (dataset-specific > dataset-category > wildcard)
  - “legal hold” acts as an override on enforcement (evaluation surfaces it explicitly) and prevents deletion jobs from acting on held datasets.
- Normalization + determinism:
  - Canonical sort order for selectors and scopes to avoid drift in JSON output and caching keys.
  - Stable JSON marshal for effective policy snapshots (used by Console/status and evidence capture).
- Guardrail enforcement hooks:
  - Evaluation can return warnings (non-fatal) vs errors (fatal) depending on caller context.
  - Explicit “no-retention” is rejected unless allow_no_delete=true is present (flag is not enabled in prod config yet; keeps us aligned with the product guardrails).
- Explain output:
  - For each effective value, record which policy document + rule produced it (scope + selector).

Testing
- Golden tests covering precedence and tricky merges (fixtures under testdata/retention/effective_policy/*.json).
- Unit tests for deterministic ordering, wildcard selector fallback, and invalid selector handling.
- Added a fuzz-ish test for “same inputs => identical effective policy JSON” to protect caching.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Wire this library into enforcement workers (ENG-2920) and telemetry TTL (ENG-2921).
- Console endpoints returning explain output (ENG-2926).

Notes
- The policy schema types are imported from the control-plane retention package added in #18422 (expected merge order: #18422 first).

conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can you spell out the precedence in code comments where the merge happens? I want this to be obvious for enforcement and Console consumers.
Jordan Lee (author): Added a block comment in merge.go above resolve() and mirrored the order in README. Also updated the golden test names so failures point to the relevant rule.

Benji Okafor (review): The region override behavior worries me. If an org-level policy defines region=us-east and tenant defines region=eu-west, how do we avoid “mixing” rules when computing an effective policy for eu-west?
Jordan Lee (author): The computation is parameterized by a target Scope (env + region). We first filter applicable documents (matching scope), then merge by specificity. A doc scoped to us-east will never be considered when evaluating eu-west. Added fixture 20-env-and-region-overrides.json to cover this.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please ensure explain output doesn’t leak policy bodies or admin notes to non-admin readers.
Jordan Lee (author): Good call. ExplainTrace currently contains (policy_id, scope, selector, field). No freeform text. Actual endpoint response shaping will be handled in ENG-2926, but I added a TODO and a test to ensure explain does not include raw JSON.

Marcus Lin (review): Legal hold semantics: does evaluation return retention_days=null or a special status? Enforcement needs to know “do not delete” without treating it like an infinite retention config.
Jordan Lee (author): Evaluation returns retention_days as configured AND a separate boolean held=true if legal_hold applies. The intent is: held=true is an enforcement override. I updated the fixture 50-legal-hold.json and README to explicitly say “hold is not a retention value.”

Leila Farouk (review): Golden tests look good. Can we add one for determinism across map iteration? We’ve been burned by nondeterministic JSON snapshots.
Jordan Lee (author): Added determinism_test.go that runs computeEffectivePolicy 200 times and asserts byte-for-byte stable JSON output.

Ethan Park (approval): LGTM after comment + test updates.
Benji Okafor (approval): Approved.
Kaitlyn Nguyen (approval): Approved, with the endpoint RBAC reminder tracked in ENG-2926.
Marcus Lin (approval): Approved.
